subject: nuclear-medicine-technology
intro: Nuclear medicine technology leads into the hospital's radioactive side — technologists who image and treat with radiopharmaceuticals, the allied imaging trades, and the technicians who monitor nuclear work.

roles.title: Nuclear Medicine Technologists
roles.what: Prepare, administer and measure radioactive isotopes in therapeutic, diagnostic and tracer studies, calculating and preparing radiopharmaceutical doses and operating radioisotope equipment on patients.
roles.where: The course runs the whole job: radiopharmaceutical production and localisation principles, gamma camera and SPECT and PET instrumentation, the bone, cardiac and thyroid scan procedures, and dose-to-patient radiation safety.

roles.title: Radiation Therapists
roles.what: Deliver radiation therapy as prescribed by a radiation oncologist: review prescriptions, prepare immobilisation and protection equipment, assist in dosimetry and tumour localisation, and keep treatment records.
roles.where: The therapy and theranostics unit — radioiodine therapy and peptide receptor therapy — plus the radiation safety unit's dose and protection rules and imaging procedures' anatomy give therapists their working toolkit.

roles.title: Radiologic Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Take x-rays and CAT scans, or administer nonradioactive materials into a patient's bloodstream for diagnostic or research purposes, positioning patients and operating imaging equipment safely.
roles.where: The instrumentation unit's detectors, image quality control, and radiation safety's dose-to-patient and pregnancy rules are shared ground with x-ray work, and the imaging procedures unit covers the cross-sectional anatomy both read.

roles.title: Nuclear Technicians
roles.what: Assist nuclear physicists and engineers in laboratory or power-generation work: operate and maintain nuclear testing and research equipment, provide quality control, and monitor radiation.
roles.where: The course's radionuclide production, gamma camera and SPECT and PET quality control, and the radioactive spills and waste topics teach the radiation monitoring and instrument QC mindset the role runs on.
